P1.evidence: Setter notes were read back properly and the prospect felt seen — 'So I spoke with Kim... I went through with your situation, the imbalance with the shoulder, you moving between New York and Maine, right?' and later 'Kim mentioned that like the belly fat, the definition' and 'kim also mentioned that like you got divorced'. That is the strongest P1a in the batch. But the four-part frame was never set and no frame agreement was sought — the rep went straight from the setter recap into content. The open question was implicit rather than asked; the prospect self-started with what he was looking for.

P2.evidence: Injuries were genuinely asked and pursued: 'maybe clarify one thing on the shoulder, has that gotten any better recently'. Diet was asked hard and well — 'Let's get real. And it's only two of us. So give me the whole truth. How does it look like right now?' plus eating-out frequency and weekends. Sleep was asked including the quality follow-up 'Yeah, but the quality' and 'when you wake up, how do you feel?', and caffeine timing was probed. Age, height, weight and body fat all arrived unprompted from the prospect rather than being asked, as did the testosterone, cholesterol, GLP-1 and NAD+ disclosures — the rep did ask 'Okay, what's the level?' on cholesterol and 'do you remember, around 500, lower, higher?' on testosterone, which is why P2c is partial rather than miss. Training week and results from current training were never asked; the rep learned the running volume only because the prospect offered it.

P3.evidence: The aesthetic goal was inherited from the setter rather than asked. The rep did bridge past the physical once, deliberately, by opening the divorce — 'that's i'm glad that you brought it up because that was my next question because kim also mentioned that like you got divorced' — which produced the deepest material in the call. But he never asked who else it impacts, and never connected the goal to the four-year-old son despite the son being raised twice; the rep supplied that link himself ('the kids are like, they're looking up to you, right?') instead of drawing it out. Reflect-back was attempted twice in weak form — 'So it's more of showing yourself that you can actually do this' and 'this is not only about, you know, losing extra pounds. Right?' — but never landed as a confirmed 'is that right?' The longevity thread was used as a closing lever ('low testosterone is strictly correlated also with your longevity') rather than surfaced as the prospect's own why.

P4.evidence: This is the phase the call actually ran, though largely because the prospect volunteered a long list: personal trainer, Flowlife programmes, GLP-1 microdosing, NAD+ injections, Viome, ChatGPT-tuned supplements, cold plunge, Russian baths, meditation. The rep did probe what happened with them ('How are you taking those supplements? Is someone, is someone actually guiding you?') and delivered the root-cause frame himself: 'if you're lacking, lacking structure around that, it's just like, you know, trying random stuff and like throwing at a wall and what will stick.' The prospect then named the gap in his own words — 'it's just actually doing it, which is where I think, like, having the accountability is good' and 'I know I can do it. It's just, yeah, it's committing and being accountable.' The scripted 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' was never asked, and the rep diagnosed rather than letting the prospect self-diagnose, which is why the phase is partial rather than hit.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The two-year question, the settle question, the 'why not' and the line in the sand were all absent. The rep substituted a fear lever of his own about testosterone and longevity — 'Low testosterone is strictly correlated also with your longevity, and I don't have to say more what's behind that' — which is a health claim used as urgency, not the scripted move, and it puts the cost of inaction in the rep's mouth rather than the prospect's.

P6.evidence: A commitment check did run before price, which is more than most calls in this batch: 'my last question is actually, if we can figure out all the technical details, are you fully committed to actually showing up and doing the' — answered 'Totally. Yeah. Yeah. I definitely am.' It conflates the belief question and the all-in question into one and never uses the 'is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' construction, so both checks are partial. The rep did correctly re-test when hesitation flickered at price, going back to belief before structuring anything — 'before we get into this, how do you feel about the program?' drawing 'I think it's good. I think I can do it', and pushing again with 'Do you think?' until he got 'Yeah. I think, I know. I know I can do it.' That is the right instinct and it is why the close held at full price.

P11.evidence: Payment link sent and a wrong-amount link caught and replaced — 'When I click on the link, it takes me to a payment that says 6,000, not three' / 'i've sent you another one' / 'I got it.' But unlike the earlier call in the same recording the rep never confirms the payment actually cleared, only 'You guys should be all set', so P11a is partial. Onboarding booked and read back from the confirmation email for July 20 3:15pm Eastern. Agreement email confirmed as arrived and the rep pushed to do it immediately with good reasoning — 'Let's get the agreement already because sometimes then you forget' — and the prospect said 'I just opened it' and 'That's done', though the collapsed diarization at that point makes a confirmed signature less than certain. Welcome email, Skool and onboarding form all covered.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger was cashflow rather than affordability — 'would love to not pay it all at once.' The rep ran the front of the play properly for once: he isolated back to belief before touching money ('before we get into this, how do you feel about the program?') and re-tested until he got a firm yes. He opened the financial picture with the monthly-surplus question — 'after the bills... how much do you have left in the tank, usually?' — but stopped at the first answer and never pinned a number, and none of the remaining financial-picture moves ran: no cash on hand, no credit cards, no available credit, no used-versus-available, no investments. The 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up' line was inverted into 'we don't have anything structured in a way that it's set in stone. We always work with clients, whatever they can do in the moment' — a materially weaker frame that concedes there is no policy before the negotiation starts. Price held at $6,000, which is the outcome that matters.

SCRIPT GAP, and the important one on this call. The prospect disclosed an unexplained neurological event with a three-day hospitalisation and paralysis, ongoing left-side weakness, prior shoulder surgery and an active neurologist. There is no scripted move for medical clearance — the playbook's only clinical acknowledgement is the known gap for a physio or surgeon who has already ruled the programme out, and it has nothing for a prospect who should be asked to get cleared before starting. The rep's improvisation ran the wrong way: 'definitely what we need to do is get you stronger around those parts', followed by a 16kg starting bell. A mandatory clearance question belongs in P2d, not in an objection play.

SCRIPT GAP. The prospect asked the rep to adjudicate his prescribed and self-administered medical regimen — GLP-1 agonists, NAD+ injections, TRT and a large supplement stack — with direct questions like 'So you think I should stop using it?' and 'Should I look into that?' The playbook gives the rep no boundary language for declining to answer, and he answered all of them. A scripted 'that is a question for your doctor, not for me' would have closed the largest compliance exposure in this batch at no cost to the sale.

notes: Commercially the strongest call in the batch: the setter handoff was used properly, discovery went genuinely deep on diet, sleep and root cause, a real commitment check ran before price, and the $6,000 held with a clean two-payment split and no uplift. The process failures are all on the clinical side — no clearance question against a three-day hospital paralysis, and the rep answering four direct medical questions he is not qualified to answer. Coach the boundary line and add a hard clearance gate to Baseline; the selling does not need fixing here, the screening does.
